name: DISCGRP.jcl
description:
This JCL job sets up the Disclosure Group VSAM file by first removing any existing version, recreating it with defined storage and key specifications, and then loading it with data from a sequential flat file. The job ensures a fresh, properly structured Disclosure Group file is available for the CardDemo application.Key Functionalities:
Deletes the existing Disclosure Group VSAM KSDS cluster (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.DISCGRP.VSAM.KSDS) to ensure a clean slate, suppressing any errors if the file does not exist.
Recreates the Disclosure Group VSAM KSDS cluster with a fixed record size of 50 bytes, a 16-byte key starting at position 0, allocated on 1 primary and 5 secondary cylinders on volume AWSHJ1, with share options (2 3) and erase-on-delete enabled.
Loads the newly created Disclosure Group VSAM file by copying all records from the sequential source file (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.DISCGRP.PS) into the VSAM KSDS cluster.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Disclosure Group VSAM cluster (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.DISCGRP.VSAM.KSDS) may or may not exist in the system prior to job execution
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The job step is triggered to initialize or refresh the Disclosure Group VSAM file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: 1. If the Disclosure Group VSAM cluster EXISTS: The entire cluster — including all its data, index, and catalog entries — is completely deleted from the system, and processing continues to the next step successfully. 2. If the Disclosure Group VSAM cluster DOES NOT EXIST: The deletion attempt fails internally, but the failure is suppressed and overridden to a success state (condition code forced to zero), and processing continues to the next step without any error or interruption. 3. In BOTH cases, the job is guaranteed to proceed to the next step — ensuring the job is safely re-runnable at any time without manual intervention.

rules.Rule_Name: STEP05 - IDCAMS - Delete Existing Disclosure Group VSAM File
rules.Rule_Description: Before creating a fresh Disclosure Group VSAM file, any previously existing Disclosure Group VSAM cluster must be fully removed from the system. This ensures a clean state before re-initialization. The process is designed to be re-runnable — if the file does not exist, the deletion failure is suppressed and processing continues normally.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The deletion of the Disclosure Group VSAM cluster has been attempted, regardless of whether the file existed or not
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The deletion step completes — either successfully or with a failure due to the file not being found
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The overall condition code for the step is forcibly set to zero (success), ensuring no downstream steps are skipped or blocked due to a deletion failure, and the job continues to the Disclosure Group VSAM file creation step

rules.Rule_Name: STEP05 - IDCAMS - Suppress Deletion Failure for Re-Runability
rules.Rule_Description: After the deletion of the Disclosure Group VSAM file is attempted, any error condition resulting from the deletion (such as file not found) must be suppressed. This policy ensures the job can be executed on a fresh system or after a previously failed run without requiring manual cleanup or intervention.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Disclosure Group master file does not yet exist in the system and needs to be established for storing Disclosure Group records
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Disclosure Group master file creation process is initiated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: A new Disclosure Group master file named 'AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.DISCGRP.VSAM.KSDS' is created as a key-sequenced indexed file, with a dedicated data component named 'AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.DISCGRP.VSAM.KSDS.DATA' for storing records and a dedicated index component named 'AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.DISCGRP.VSAM.KSDS.INDEX' for enabling fast key-based lookups

rules.Rule_Name: STEP10 - IDCAMS - Disclosure Group Master File Creation
rules.Rule_Description: Defines and creates the Disclosure Group master file as a key-indexed data store with separate data and index components to support Disclosure Group record storage and retrieval.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Disclosure Group master file is being defined with a key structure
Acceptance_Criteria.When: A Disclosure Group record is stored in or retrieved from the master file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Each Disclosure Group record must carry a unique 16-character identifier starting at the first byte (position 0) of the record; any attempt to store a record with a duplicate 16-character key must be rejected to maintain uniqueness of Disclosure Group entries

rules.Rule_Name: STEP10 - IDCAMS - Disclosure Group Record Unique Key Identification
rules.Rule_Description: Enforces that every Disclosure Group record is uniquely identified by a 16-character key located at the very beginning of the record, ensuring no duplicate Disclosure Group entries exist.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Disclosure Group master file is defined with a fixed record size requirement
Acceptance_Criteria.When: A Disclosure Group record is written to or read from the master file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Every Disclosure Group record must be exactly 50 bytes in length; both the minimum and maximum allowable record size is fixed at 50 bytes, and records that do not conform to this size must not be accepted into the Disclosure Group master file

rules.Rule_Name: STEP10 - IDCAMS - Disclosure Group Fixed Record Size Enforcement
rules.Rule_Description: Enforces a strict fixed-length record structure for all Disclosure Group records, ensuring every record stored in the master file is exactly 50 bytes — no more, no less.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Disclosure Group master file is defined with a mandatory data erasure policy
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Disclosure Group master file is deleted from the system
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All Disclosure Group records and associated data must be physically erased from the storage media — not merely logically removed — ensuring that sensitive Disclosure Group information cannot be recovered, reconstructed, or accessed by any means after deletion

rules.Rule_Name: STEP10 - IDCAMS - Disclosure Group Sensitive Data Erasure on Deletion
rules.Rule_Description: Enforces a data security policy requiring that all Disclosure Group data is physically erased from storage media whenever the Disclosure Group master file is deleted, preventing any recovery of sensitive disclosure information.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Disclosure Group master file is being accessed by one or more programs or users at the same time
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Concurrent read or write requests are made against the Disclosure Group master file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Multiple programs must be permitted to read the Disclosure Group master file simultaneously without restriction; write access must be controlled so that only one program can update the file at a time within the same system (SHAREOPTIONS 2), while across multiple systems, concurrent read and write operations are permitted (SHAREOPTIONS 3), preventing data corruption during simultaneous access

rules.Rule_Name: STEP10 - IDCAMS - Disclosure Group Concurrent Access Control
rules.Rule_Description: Defines the concurrent access permissions for the Disclosure Group master file, allowing multiple programs to read simultaneously while enforcing controlled write access to protect data integrity.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A sequential flat file (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.DISCGRP.PS) exists and contains Disclosure Group records, AND a freshly created empty Disclosure Group VSAM KSDS (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.DISCGRP.VSAM.KSDS) is available and ready to receive data
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Disclosure Group data load process is triggered
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Every Disclosure Group record from the sequential flat file must be copied into the VSAM KSDS without any filtering, transformation, or omission — the VSAM file must contain a complete and exact replica of all records from the source flat file, automatically organized in key sequence within the VSAM structure

rules.Rule_Name: STEP15 - IDCAMS REPRO - Load All Disclosure Group Records from Flat File into VSAM
rules.Rule_Description: This step copies all Disclosure Group records from the sequential master flat file into the operational VSAM Key-Sequenced Dataset, making the Disclosure Group data available for key-based lookups by downstream applications.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Disclosure Group data load process is initiated AND the source sequential flat file (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.DISCGRP.PS) is referenced as the input
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Records are being read from the source Disclosure Group flat file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The source flat file (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.DISCGRP.PS) must be accessed in read-only shared mode — its contents must NOT be altered, deleted, or locked exclusively, ensuring the source data remains intact and available to other users or processes during the load

rules.Rule_Name: STEP15 - IDCAMS REPRO - Protect Source Disclosure Group Flat File During Load
rules.Rule_Description: The source Disclosure Group sequential flat file must remain unmodified and accessible to other processes during the data load operation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Disclosure Group data load process is initiated AND the target VSAM KSDS (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.DISCGRP.VSAM.KSDS) is referenced as the output destination
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Records are being written into the Disclosure Group VSAM KSDS
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The target VSAM file (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.DISCGRP.VSAM.KSDS) must be held under exclusive access — no other program or user is permitted to read from or write to the Disclosure Group VSAM file until the load operation is fully completed, guaranteeing that the loaded data is consistent and uncorrupted

rules.Rule_Name: STEP15 - IDCAMS REPRO - Exclusive Access Control on Target Disclosure Group VSAM During Load
rules.Rule_Description: The target Disclosure Group VSAM file must be exclusively locked during the data load to prevent concurrent access conflicts and ensure data integrity of the loaded records.
